title: Negroni
intro: Equal parts gin, Campari and sweet vermouth: bitter, sweet and dry in balance.

steps.t: Fill a rocks glass with ice to chill it.
Pour the gin, Campari and vermouth into a mixing glass (or tall glass) full of ice.
Stir with a bar spoon for 20–30 seconds, until the glass feels cold.
Empty the rocks glass, add fresh ice and strain in the drink.
Garnish with half an orange slice.

tips.t: Swap the gin for prosecco and it becomes a Sbagliato.
Use bourbon instead of gin for a rounder Boulevardier.
Use one large ice cube: it melts slowly and won't water the drink down.

title: Dry Martini
intro: Ice-cold gin and a touch of dry vermouth, stirred until crystal clear.

steps.t: Put the martini glass in the freezer for 10 minutes.
steps.label: Glass

steps.t: Meanwhile, fill a mixing glass with ice and pour in the vermouth, then the gin.
Stir with a bar spoon for 30 seconds: stirred, not shaken, it stays clear.
Strain into the frozen glass.
Twist the lemon peel over the drink to release its oils and drop it in, or use the olive.

tips.t: Keep the gin in the freezer: the Martini stays ice-cold with less dilution.
20 ml vermouth makes it softer; cocktail onions instead of olive make a Gibson.
Serve with salted almonds or green olives.

title: Old Fashioned
intro: Bourbon, sugar and bitters: the oldest cocktail, stirred slowly over ice.

steps.t: Put the sugar cube in a rocks glass and soak it with the bitters and a teaspoon of water.
Crush it with a muddler and stir until the sugar has almost dissolved.
Add the large ice cube and pour in the bourbon.
Stir with a bar spoon for 30 seconds to chill and slightly dilute.
Twist the orange peel over the glass, rub it round the rim and drop it in.

tips.t: A bar spoon of demerara syrup instead of the cube dissolves instantly.
Rye whiskey makes it drier and spicier.
Pairs well with dark chocolate or toasted walnuts.

title: Margarita
intro: Tequila, fresh lime and triple sec, shaken hard, with a salted rim.

steps.t: Run a lime wedge round the outer rim of the glass and dip it in salt.
Squeeze the rest of the lime: you need 25 ml juice.
Pour the tequila, triple sec and lime juice into a shaker full of ice.
Shake hard for 12–15 seconds, until the shaker is frosty outside.
Strain into the glass over fresh ice, or into a coupe without ice.

tips.t: Tommy's Margarita: 15 ml agave syrup instead of the triple sec.
Salt only half the rim, so each sip can be salty or not.
Frozen: blend everything with 150 g ice until slushy.

title: Mojito
intro: White rum, lime, mint and cane sugar over crushed ice: the Cuban classic.

steps.t: Cut the half lime into wedges and put it in a highball glass with the mint and sugar.
Muddle gently: press the lime but don't shred the mint, or it turns bitter.
Pour in the rum and stir until the sugar dissolves.
Fill with crushed ice and churn from the bottom up with a bar spoon.
Top with soda water, add more ice and garnish with a mint sprig.

tips.t: Leave out the rum and add strawberries for a strawberry Nojito.
Slap the mint sprig against your palm before garnishing to release its aroma.

title: Daiquiri
intro: Just white rum, lime and sugar: the crisp, dry Cuban sour.

steps.t: Chill a coupe in the freezer or by filling it with ice.
Juice the lime and measure 25 ml.
Pour the rum, lime juice and syrup into a shaker full of ice.
Shake hard for 12–15 seconds, until the shaker is frosty.
Empty the coupe and strain through a fine strainer to catch ice shards.

tips.t: Simple syrup: dissolve equal weights of sugar and water over heat, then cool.
Frozen strawberry version: blend with 100 g strawberries and 150 g ice.

title: Whiskey Sour
intro: Bourbon, lemon and an egg white that dry-shakes into a silky foam.

ing.n: egg white from a very fresh egg

steps.t: Juice the lemon and pour 25 ml juice, the bourbon, syrup and egg white into an empty shaker.
Shake hard for 15 seconds without ice: the egg white whips into foam.
Add ice and shake for another 12 seconds, until the shaker is frosty.
Strain through a fine strainer into a rocks glass over fresh ice.
Let the foam settle for a few seconds and dot it with 3 drops of bitters.

tips.t: Vegan version: swap the egg white for 20 ml aquafaba (chickpea water).
New York Sour: float 20 ml red wine over the foam.

title: Moscow Mule
intro: Vodka, lime and spicy ginger beer in a copper mug that keeps it ice-cold.

steps.t: Fill a copper mug, or a highball glass, with ice.
Squeeze half the lime straight into the mug and slice the other half.
Pour in the vodka, then the ginger beer.
Stir gently just once from the bottom with a bar spoon, to keep the fizz.
Garnish with a lime slice and serve at once.

tips.t: Use homemade ginger soda instead of bottled ginger beer.
Swap the vodka for dark rum and it's a Dark 'n' Stormy.

title: Cosmopolitan
intro: Citrus vodka, Cointreau, cranberry and lime: pink, dry and zesty.

steps.t: Chill a martini glass by filling it with ice and water.
Juice the half lime and pour 15 ml into a shaker full of ice.
Add the vodka, Cointreau and cranberry juice and shake hard for 12 seconds.
Empty the glass and strain in through a fine strainer.
Twist the orange peel over the drink, rub the rim and rest it on the glass.

tips.t: If your cranberry juice is unsweetened, add 10 ml simple syrup.

title: Espresso Martini
intro: Vodka, coffee liqueur and fresh espresso, shaken to a dense crema.

steps.t: Make the espresso and let it cool slightly while you chill the glass with ice and water.
Pour the vodka, coffee liqueur, espresso and syrup into a shaker full of ice.
Shake very hard for 15 seconds: the force is what builds the foam.
Empty the glass and strain in through a fine strainer.
Let the crema settle and float 3 coffee beans in the centre.

tips.t: No espresso machine? Use moka pot coffee, taking the first, thickest part.
The fresher the espresso, the thicker and longer-lasting the foam.

title: Pisco sour
intro: Pisco, lime and egg white shaken to a silky foam, finished with Angostura.

steps.t: Chill the glass and squeeze the lime: you need 30 ml of juice.
Pour the pisco, lime juice, syrup and egg white into a shaker and shake hard for 15 seconds without ice to build foam.
Add ice and shake again for 15 seconds, until the shaker is frosty.
Strain into the chilled glass and let the foam settle for a few seconds.
Dot 3 drops of Angostura on the foam and serve immediately.

tips.t: The dry shake without ice whips the egg white so the foam lasts to the last sip.
Egg-free: use 20 ml aquafaba, the liquid from canned chickpeas, for the same foam.
For a chilcano, top pisco and half a lime's juice with ginger ale over ice.

title: Kir
intro: Burgundy white wine and crème de cassis: the aperitif born in Dijon.

ing.n: well-chilled Bourgogne Aligoté (or another dry white)

steps.t: Keep the wine and crème de cassis in the fridge and chill a wine glass.
Pour the crème de cassis into the bottom of the glass.
Top up slowly with the cold white wine: it mixes almost by itself, no ice needed.
Give it a gentle stir with a teaspoon and serve at once, with gougères or nibbles.

tips.t: Kir royal: swap the wine for champagne or a Crémant de Bourgogne.
Made with a young, fruity red such as Beaujolais, it becomes a Cardinal.
Look for crème de cassis in wine shops; once opened keep it in the fridge and it lasts for months.

title: Mint Julep
intro: Bourbon, fresh mint and a mound of crushed ice: the Kentucky Derby drink.

steps.t: Put the mint leaves and syrup in a julep cup or rocks glass and press gently, without mashing them to a pulp.
Add the bourbon and half-fill the glass with crushed ice; stir until the outside of the glass frosts.
Top with more crushed ice in a dome and stir for a few more seconds.
Slap the mint sprig against your palm to release its aroma, tuck it in beside a short straw and serve.

tips.t: Finely crushed ice is everything: wrap ice cubes in a tea towel and bash them with a rolling pin.
Swap the bourbon for cognac and you have the 19th-century julep.
